question: A pyramid has a base area of 60 cm² and height 9 cm. What is its volume?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The volume of any pyramid is directly one-third of the product of its base area and height.

Volume = (1 ÷ 3) × Base Area × Height

Volume = (1 ÷ 3) × 60 × 9 = 180 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 180 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base Area of the pyramid = 60 cm²

Height of the pyramid = 9 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a Pyramid = (1 ÷ 3) × Base Area × Height

 h = 9 cm
 Base Area = 60 sq. cm

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = 20 × 9

⇒ Volume = 180 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 180 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prism vs Pyramid Volume

The volume of a prism is directly calculated as Base Area × Height, whereas a pyramid's volume is exactly one-third of the prism's volume having the same base and height.

Total Surface Area of a Pyramid

Total Surface Area = Lateral Surface Area + Base Area. For a regular pyramid, Lateral Surface Area = (1 ÷ 2) × Base Perimeter × Slant Height.

Cone as a Pyramid

A cone is a specific type of pyramid with a circular base. Its volume formula is exactly (1 ÷ 3) × πr²h, which follows the same foundational logic.
